Description
The Austrian Philharmonic platinum coin is the most popular coin series from the European continent. Austrian Philharmonic Platinum coins were first released in 2016 in the hopes to honor the greatness that is the Vienna Philharmonic Orchestra. Although these Austrian Platinum coins have a face value of €100, they are worth a great deal more for their high Platinum content. This 1 oz  Austrian Philharmonic Platinum coin is a highly recognizable, stunning, and precious platinum coin that can strengthen your precious metal portfolio.
Like many of the other Austrian coins that are on the market today, the Philharmonic coins represent an incredible investment as well as an artistic piece. This 1 oz Austrian Philharmonic Platinum coin is struck with 1 troy oz of .9995 pure platinum. Since these coins have such a good quantity of pure platinum in them, they are mostly used for investment purposes by people who are looking to hedge against inflation or convert their wealth to an easily transferred form of wealth. The year of mintage of the 1 oz Austrian Philharmonic platinum Coin may vary depending on the availability of the coin in our inventory
Design of 1 Oz Platinum Austrian Philharmonic Coin
The Austrian Philharmonic platinum coin is a design masterpiece. The obverse of the 1 oz Austrian Philharmonic platinum coin features the depiction of the Great Organ of the Golden Hall in one of Austria’s most famous concert halls, the Musikverein. Above the great organ of the coin, is the inscription of  “REPUBLIK OSTERREICH” which means “The Republic of Austria” in English. Below the Great Organ, you can see “ 1 UNZE PLATIN 999.5” along with the year of issue and denomination.
On the reverse of the 1 oz Austrian platinum Philharmonic coin, you can see the depiction of an array of musical instruments carved in great detail. The musical instruments include a French horn, bassoon, harp, cello, and four violins. The inscription of the phrase “WIENER PHILHARMONIKER” can be seen just above the musical instruments.
